item.title: MTN Bushfire 2025 boosts eSwatini economy by $7m, university study finds
item.description: A newly released Economic Impact Assessment by South Africa’s North-West University (NWU) has found that the MTN Bushfire 2025 festival generated E121.2 million (about $7 500 700) for eSwatini’s economy, highlighting the event’s significance beyond arts and culture. item.title: Apple Music, YouTube launch AI playlist tools
item.description: Apple Music and YouTube Music have introduced new AI-powered playlist features that allow users to generate personalised music selections using text or voice prompts. YouTube Music recently rolled out its AI Playlist feature for Premium subscribers in the U.S. and select international markets. The tool enables users to create playlists based on mood, genre, ideas, release periods, or similar-sounding tracks. item.title: Donald, Amanda Black reunite for soulful Valentine’s duet Amanga
item.description: Donald and Amanda Black, two of South Africa’s most revered voices, finally come together on ‘Amanga’, an R&B-infused Afro-soul track released on the eve of Valentine’s Day. At a time when many vocalists exchange depth for trend-driven hip hop flows and call it “evolution,” this collaboration is a quiet, unhurried corrective: honest, intoxicating, and profoundly human. item.title: Sony unveils AI tool aimed at detecting use of copyrighted works
item.description: Sony Group has disclosed a new artificial intelligence detection tool designed to identify the use of protected works in AI-generated content, according to a recent report by Nikkei Asia. Developed by Sony’s AI division, the technology is said to function across multiple media formats, including music, film and video games. item.title: Apple Music maintains lower pricing as rivals raise subscription fees
item.description: Apple Music is maintaining its current subscription prices in the United States, creating a widening cost gap with competitors Spotify and Amazon Music as rivals implement recent increases. Apple Music’s Individual plan remains priced at $10.99 per month, compared with $12.99 charged by Spotify and Amazon Music. item.title: Open call: Marafiki Arts Festival 2026
item.description: The organisers of the Marafiki Arts Festival in Tanzania have opened submissions for the 2026 edition, inviting performing artists from across Africa to participate. The festival, now in its sixth year, celebrates creativity, culture, and diverse artistic expression. Submission details Artists and groups interested in participating must submit their applications by 20 February. item.title: Southern African arts organisations launch regional incubator network
item.description: House On Fire in eSwatini, AltBlk Continua in South Africa, and The X-Hub in Mozambique have joined forces to launch the Arts Incubator Corridor (AIC), a regional network designed to accelerate creative development, innovation, and market access across Southern Africa. The initiative brings together three established creative platforms to provide a structured framework for training, mentorship, business incubation, and cross-border collaboration for emerging and established artists. item.title: Wandile Mbambeni on faith, storytelling and the power of live connection
item.description: By Tshifhiwa Mungoni and Sibongile Kobo South African singer-songwriter Wandile Mbambeni has built a quietly distinctive career rooted in soul, storytelling and live performance. A multifaceted musician whose work has travelled well beyond South Africa’s borders, Mbambeni continues to shape a sound that draws from country-blues, folk and Afro-soul, while remaining deeply personal. item.title: Pro Heed’s ‘This Feeling’ becomes a Valentine’s season anthem
item.description: One of the most unconventional and interactive love song campaigns in recent memory, Pro Heed’s ‘This Feeling’ has captured hearts, amassing over half a million streams across platforms. More than just a song, it has evolved into a full-fledged celebration of love, spanning weddings, Valentine’s Day events, and even a signature fragrance line. item.title: Joburg Theatre presents ‘An Ode to Motown’ for Black History Month
item.description: Joburg Theatre will host An Ode to Motown from 21 February to 1 March 2026, a theatrical production celebrating the music and legacy of Motown Records. The show forms part of the theatre’s Black History Month programme, presenting a combination of live music, storytelling, and choreography.
